name: Scalp exfoliation

lead: Scalp exfoliation uses scrubs or acids to remove dead skin and buildup. People use it for flaking and hoping for healthier hair.
Salicylic acid is an approved dandruff active, but no trials tested exfoliation for hair growth.

paras: Physical granules rub debris off; acids such as salicylic or glycolic acid loosen bonds between dead skin cells.
Descriptions say overdoing it may cause dryness, oiliness or irritation, and that people with psoriasis, eczema or open sores should consult a dermatologist.

Scrub shampoo and pre-shampoo scrub cleanser

lead: Scalp exfoliation is a hair-care practice that uses physical scrubs, chemical exfoliants such as salicylic or glycolic acid, or hybrids to remove dead skin cells, oil and product buildup from the scalp.[1] Proponents say it reduces flaking, helps products absorb and supports hair growth.[1]

Salicylic acid is an FDA-approved over-the-counter anti-dandruff active, and dandruff shampoos combine actives such as zinc pyrithione and ketoconazole.[2] Physical scalp scrubs are not covered in that reference.[2]
One 2024 study evaluated a hydroxy acid scrub combined with a copper tripeptide serum in adults with seborrheic dermatitis.[3] No studies were found testing scalp exfoliation for hair growth.
infobox: Salt, sugar, charcoal; salicylic, glycolic, lactic acids[1]
Less flaking, clearer follicles, better product absorption[1]

paras: Physical exfoliants use granules such as sugar, sea salt or charcoal, rubbed in with massage. Chemical exfoliants use acids that dissolve bonds between dead skin cells.[1]

Descriptions claim exfoliation unclogs follicles and supports hair growth.[1] Dermatology references on dandruff describe cause as involving sebum, Malassezia yeasts and individual sensitivity, and list antifungal and keratolytic shampoos as treatments.[2]
Descriptions say over-exfoliation may disrupt the scalp barrier, causing dryness, extra oil or discomfort, and suggest people with psoriasis, eczema or open sores consult a dermatologist.[1]

A 2024 study in Cureus assessed the safety, efficacy and tolerability of a regimen combining a hydroxy acid scrub with a copper tripeptide serum for seborrheic dermatitis in adults.[3] No studies were found on exfoliation alone for hair growth or density.
